# webzjs (Zcash wallet, WebAssembly)

ChainSafe/WebZjs at `a50df944c32243cb8da9f86e7d52cb65ac926439`, built by `ops/build_webzjs.sh` (nightly-2025-06-20, clang 18.1.8, wasm-bindgen-cli 0.2.100, two import patches).
Only this README, `SHA256SUMS` and `BUILD_INFO` (patch sha256, commit, tool versions, "UNVERIFIED BUILD" marker for `PKG_DIR` builds) are in git; the 58 MB wasm and the generated JS are rebuilt with the script and checked against `SHA256SUMS`:

    cd web/vendor/webzjs && sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS    # macOS: shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS

Used only by `web/zec-hop.js`, loaded on demand. Needs a cross-origin isolated page (COOP/COEP, see `ops/nginx-stealth-zec.conf`).

Integrity pin, honestly: `loadZjs` compares the glue and the wasm with hashes that live in `web/zec-hop.js`, served from the same origin as the files. That protects against a stale, mixed or partially swapped vendor directory, NOT against a compromised origin (whoever can change the files can change the hashes). Pinning the hashes outside the origin (or SRI on the module graph, including the four `snippets/` scripts) is not done yet.

Scope of the memory-wallet patch, honestly: the "unscanned range" test (`note_in_unscanned_range`) applies to Sapling notes only (the scan queue is mapped to Sapling tree positions); for Orchard and Ironwood notes it never excludes anything, so a note behind an unscanned gap is counted and selected and fails when its witness is built. Note selection stops at the target per pool; with notes in several pools of `sources` the total can exceed it, and if the eligible notes fall short they are all returned (the caller's InsufficientFunds check decides). `ops/check_repro.sh` measures reproducibility (two builds in different dirs); BUILD_INFO does not claim it. The wasm-opt that wasm-pack downloads at build time is not pinned.

"verified build" in BUILD_INFO, exactly (1123 L-4): the build run checked the patch sha256, the WebZjs commit, the sha256 of the clang tarball and of the rustup installer, and the exact version STRINGS of rustc (nightly-2025-06-20), clang, just, wasm-pack and wasm-bindgen-cli (a version string, not a hash of the binary). NOT pinned: the wasm-opt that wasm-pack downloads, the stable rustc that compiles just / wasm-pack / wasm-bindgen-cli, and the binaries of those tools. So "verified" does not mean that a third party gets the same wasm bytes. The committed BUILD_INFO of the current vendor files was written by an earlier wording of the script and is not regenerated here (that would need a rebuild); the wording above and in `ops/build_webzjs.sh` is what a new build writes. `ops/check_repro.sh` builds twice with separate WORK, cargo/rustup, wasm-pack and XDG caches; a PASS covers wasm-opt drift between the two downloads only, not over time.

Accepted residuals (audit 1123 round 4; nothing was changed in the vendor files or the pins for these):
- L-1, worker threads fetch their scripts again, unpinned. `loadZjs` hashes the bytes the main thread runs and rewrites the worker-spawning URLs to the absolute vendor URLs, but the workers that the thread pool starts fetch `workerHelpers.js`, `web_worker_module.bundler.js` and `webzjs_wallet.js` themselves, without a hash check. Accepted because these are same-origin files under the hash-checked deploy (`ops/deploy_lab.sh` refuses files that do not match `SHA256SUMS`), and the pin never claimed to stop an origin or a cache that serves different bytes to different requests; that is the "compromised origin" case already stated above. Not fixable without handing the workers verified blobs, which means changing the vendored glue and so a rebuild.
- L-2, errors from `note_is_spendable` make note selection and `spendable_notes_meta` all-or-nothing (one orphaned note in the in-memory DB fails every selection for that account until the wallet is rebuilt). Accepted: the old behaviour silently treated such a note as unspendable, which hides a corrupt state and could under-report a balance; failing loudly is the safe direction. The failure is a visible error (the hop step halts or retries); no funds move because of it, and the hop wallet's keys are derived from the payment's key, so the wallet can be recreated.
- L-3, Orchard / Ironwood notes behind an unscanned gap can be selected and fail late, when the witness is built (`note_in_unscanned_range` is Sapling-only, see above). Accepted: the late failure surfaces as an error from the proposal / build step, before anything is broadcast; in `SEND_OUT` (`web/zec-hop.js`) `p.raw` is set only after `create_proposed_transactions` returned, and the broadcast comes after that, so a failure at witness time happens before anything is sent and the step retries or halts. This was read in the code, not exercised against the real wasm.
